posts.headline: The 2026 Schedule Is Here. Four Games Will Define It.
posts.body: Da Dangsters host Pacific Pigskins in Week 1. Computer Jocks face the defending champs in Week 9. And the final week? All eight division titles on the line.
content: Boom! The 2026 schedule for The League is official, and I'm told the league office got this one right. One hundred forty-four games. Fourteen weeks. Four doubleheader weeks that dodge every NFL bye in the book. And four marquee matchups that will live in your draft prep, your waiver moves, and your playoff prayers.

Let's start where every season starts: Week 1, Da Dangsters at Pacific Pigskins. This is a division rivalry, opening week, doubleheader week—the setup every franchise circles on release day. Money is nice, but championships are better, and the team that punches first in this league sets the tone for everything that follows. Pacific Pigskins and Da Dangsters have met 25 times under the current ownership, and Pacific Pigskins leads the series 14-11. They know what's at stake.

Now flip to Week 4. Bring the Pain travels to Vitside Mafia for Throwback Week—old-school uniforms, the kind of game that reminds you why you fell in love with this league in the first place. These two have squared off 15 times, and Vitside Mafia holds a 8-7 edge. League sources tell me this is the game everyone will be texting about come Week 5.

Week 9: Computer Jocks at Dark Magicians of Chaos. This is the championship rematch. Last year's title game, running it back in the middle of the season. These franchises have played 28 times—dead even at 14-14. That's the kind of symmetry that makes you believe in fate, or at least in a schedule that was built to separate the contenders from the pretenders.

And then Week 14. Running Down The Dream at Wascawy Wabbits, with a division title on the line in the final week. Not a tiebreaker. Not a coin flip. A game. That's how you finish a season: with stakes so clear that every decision made before kickoff matters. All eight division games are decided in Week 14—the league office made sure of that.

The rivalry renewals are stacked this season. Dark Magicians of Chaos at Wascawy Wabbits in Week 1—28 meetings, dead even at 14-14. Dark Magicians of Chaos at Running Down The Dream in Week 2—26 meetings, also knotted at 13-13. Pacific Pigskins at Vitside Mafia in Week 3—35 meetings, Vitside Mafia up 19-16. Dark Magicians of Chaos at Fire Ready Aim in Week 3—35 meetings, Fire Ready Aim leading 21-14. These are the feuds that built this league. These are the teams that know each other inside out.

The construction here is clean. Eighty-seven pairings in this schedule have met six times or more—that's history playing out across sixteen weeks. Bye-week luck is nearly even, the gap between the most and least favored franchise is four, and the league made sure 40 of a possible 48 division games land in weeks with no NFL byes. No two division rivals meet twice inside nine weeks of each other. That's not luck. That's architecture.

Your 2026 season begins Week 1 with Da Dangsters at Pacific Pigskins. Circle it. Book your whole season around it. Everything else flows from there. The full schedule, week by week, is on the schedule release page.

posts.headline: Cut Watch: Procrastinators Face Deadline Reckoning
posts.body: Da Dangsters, Maverick, and Running down the Dream haven't filed cutdown plans — and the system is about to make brutal choices for them. Three other teams already have their affairs in order.
content: Boom! We've got three teams staring down the barrel of an unfiled cutdown plan, and let me tell you, that's a recipe for disaster. Da Dangsters, Maverick, and Running down the Dream — you're all two over the limit, and the clock is ticking. Pacific Pigskins, Midwestside Connection, and Bring The Pain already have their picks marked and ready to go. That's how you do business. The rest of you? You're about to learn a hard lesson about the mechanical nature of this deadline.

Here's the gut-punch for the procrastinators: if you don't file a cutdown plan, the system doesn't care about your best judgment. It won't target the weakest blended ADP or the highest salary. No — it goes NEWEST PICKUP FIRST. Da Dangsters, if you do nothing, you're losing QB Jameis Winston (auction win Aug 11) and WR Tee Higgins (auction win Mar 23). Running down the Dream faces the same nightmare: QB Davis Mills and TE David Njoku both vanish. That's not strategic roster management — that's financial self-harm. Maverick, you've got two rookies that can taxi to the practice squad, which buys you time, but don't sleep on it.

For the teams that DID file plans — Pacific Pigskins at 25 active, Midwestside Connection at 25, and Bring The Pain at 24 — you're already cutting. But let's talk about who you SHOULD be eyeing, because salary and value matter when you're making the hard calls. Pacific Pigskins: QB Jalen Milroe, WR Savion Williams, and TE Cade Stover are all unranked, dead weight at four and three years. Easy cuts. That Def the Las Vegas Raiders defense? Same story — unranked, $625K, and nobody in this league drafts a bottom-tier unit. Midwestside Connection, you're looking at PK Joshua Karty and QB Will Howard as the cleanest paycuts — both unranked, sub-$500K, contracts that don't sting. RB Kareem Hunt at $750K on a one-year deal is tougher because you're eating a higher salary, but redraft value is everything on year-one deals. Money is nice, but championships are better — don't overpay for scraps.

Maverick, I'm told you're sitting on 11 wide receivers. Eleven! Your WR room is bloated, and Tyreek Hill ($1.650M), Xavier Legette ($1.210M), and Ja'Lynn Polk ($847K) are all unranked in league ADP — nobody wants them. John Metchie at $425K and four years is the softest cut of the bunch. Get those two rookies on taxi, then get aggressive with the deadwood. Da Dangsters, your RB Jarquez Hunter and WR Cedric Tillman are both unranked — clean surgical cuts. But if you don't act, you're hemorrhaging WR Tee Higgins instead, and that's a championship killer. File a plan. File it NOW.

The lesson here is brutal and simple: procrastination at The League deadline doesn't forgive. You don't get to hold onto your targets while the system eats your best recent acquisitions. Three teams have already locked in their cuts with forethought and discipline. Three teams are about to get punished for sleeping on the job. Tick tock.
